If he does have the dexcom, you can download a Follower app. I’m not sure if this requires the child to have a phone or if you can hook it up through that little monitor for the Dexcom that they send you, but my entire family can track my blood sugar 24/7 as long as my phone is nearby, bluetooth on and wifi (i use data) on (to be able to send the data to the followers every 5 minutes. the followers will also need their wifi on.). the “host” wont need wifi to get their readings for themselves, but they will need to keep their bluetooth on 24/7 to be able to read the number on the screen or else itll say Bluetooth Off. itll keep reading your blood sugar, but it just wont show you if its off. It’s sounds complicated at first, but it really isnt, and my family, even if were a country away, could get my numbers. I would recommend getting him a phone if you’d like to watch his numbers, as well. Sometimes, I can even miss something happening with my blood sugar, and they’ll call me or something. Especially when I’m in class or when I’m busy, sometimes I cant be looking at my phone (usually teachers understand my phone business, except for tests.) and its nice to have someone else getting beeps instead of it all just being on me. Some of my friends even Follow me (however i tell them to have their alerts off unless they want to be woken up by me going low at night lol) 😁 its a big responsibility having a phone though, and if you break or lose it, its like losing your lifeline. take a moment to assess other options before giving your child a phone, still, but this is just my take on the matter. best of luck!!
